def: The tree of nodes that Python builds from source text, in which each node is a small part of the program and children sit inside their parents.
One part of a syntax tree, such as a name, a number, an operator or a whole function definition.
Turning source text into a syntax tree, which in Python is done by ast.parse.
A class with one method per node type that walks a syntax tree and keeps notes without changing it.
A visitor whose methods return replacement nodes, so that it can rewrite a syntax tree.
A list of the only things allowed, such as the node types a candidate program may contain, so that anything not listed is refused.
Code that nobody has read or vouched for, such as a randomly mutated or model-written program, which must be checked before it runs.
The interpreter's internal, ready-to-run form of a program, made by compile and run by exec.
A dictionary that maps names to values and decides which names the code run inside it can see.
The names Python gives every program without an import, such as len, open and __import__, which a restricted namespace can replace with a short list.
A limit on the number of steps a candidate may take, counted by ticks injected into its code, so that endless loops end without a clock.
A function the interpreter calls on events such as each new line, which can be used to count the work a program does.
A standard version of a program in which meaningless differences such as variable names and docstrings are removed, so equal programs give equal text.
A change to a program that alters its code but leaves its score the same.
